newsitem.title: UK: Easynet thinks big as subscriber base grows.
newsitem.headline: Easynet thinks big as subscriber base grows.

text.p: Easynet Group pledged on Monday to stay one step ahead of its competitors as the UK Internet service provider, that was floated in March, announced that its subscriber base had swollen 150 percent to 7,500 since January.
"We believe we are already a main internet provider -- one of the top three," chairman and chief executive David Rowe told Reuters in an interview.
"We'd like to carry on forever and gain 100 percent of the market -- but that's probably unrealistic," he added.

Blaming a high level of investment in company infrastructure and the national network, Easynet -- which is floated on the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) -- saw first half pretax losses more than double to 244,133 stg from 100,730, while turnover surged 450 percent to around 627,000 stg.

Easynet, which also creates, maintains and designs websites, offers services to both the flat fee, low margin consumer market and the corporate market -- which represents about 40 percent of overall revenues.
To gain access to the global Internet network, users have to pay a provider a monthly rental charge giving them access to the lines owned or rented by the provider.
There are about 160 service providers in Britain fighting for revenue in a market that some industry experts say will be worth almost one billion stg by the millennium.
Easynet said it had now completed a national Internet infrastructure which offers local-call Internet access throughout Britain as well as 100 percent coverage in France.

Rowe sees the group's main rivals as being Demon, which serves about half the UK's Internet users, MFS Communications of the U.S. -- which is merging with WorldCom, the fourth largest U.S. long-distance operator -- and British Telecommunications.

But Rowe said he was not daunted by the presence of huge companies that have the cash to invest up front and compete on price and quality of service. "We are focused on the Internet and...we have a lot of expertise in the business," he said.
In the next year, Rowe expects the "convergence theory" of voice and data, whereby Internet users can speak on local-rate calls to each other over computers, to become a viable product.

"We'll see "voice' rearing its head in the next 12 months on the Internet...If one has a fairy low-cost network and is able to drive voice across it -- it is a tremendous threat to people like BT in the long-term," he added.

Easynet expects the rate of infrastructure investment to fall and revenues to rise substantially with corporate business increasing in importance as a source of overall revenue. It also wants to forge new alliances and develop new products this year.
Easynet said it did not intend to pay a dividend until profits "justify payment". But it stated: "The board looks forward to the rest of the year with great confidence."
